newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's crude oil production rises - Pemex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's crude oil production rises - Pemex.

text.p: Mexico's state-owned oil and gas company, Petroleos Mexicanos, said in a report Thursday its crude oil production rose 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) in November to an average 2.859 million bpd.
November output compared with an average 2.858 million bpd, and above an average 2.854 million bpd during the first 11 months of the year.
Production of heavy Maya crude rose to 1.395 million bpd from 1.379 million bpd, while production fell slightly in Pemex's light Isthmus and extra-light Olmeca.
Exports of crude oil fell to 1.499 million bpd for November from 1.657 million bpd the month before.
Natural gas production for November fell to 4.154 billion cubic feet per day (cfd), down an average 22 bpd from the previous month and down from the year's average 4.19 billion cfd, the company said.

Pemex's petrochemical output rose slightly in November to 1.37 million tonnes from 1.368 million tonnes the previous month as ammonium and benzene output increased and ethylene fell. The company's petrochemical output is still below 1996 average monthly levels of 1.537 million tonnes.
Mexico exported 53,800 tonnes of petrochemicals at a value of $8.2 million in November, and did not import any petrochemicals. In 1996, imports ranged between 43,200 and 150,500 tonnes.
In November, the country exported 107,400 bpd of natural gas and petroleum by-products and imported 195,900 bpd, mostly gasolines and liquid petroleum gas, Pemex said.
